headlines.title: Authorities investigate another possible mountain lion sighting in San Francisco
headlines.description: A mountain lion sighting near Fell and Baker Saturday night prompted a big response. On Sunday, Animal Care and Control said the threat appears to be over; however, authorities said there was an unconfirmed mountain lion sighting on Sunday. Peter Tira with the California Department of Fish and Wildlife says they were among those called in on Saturday, but never actually saw a mountain lion. They monitored the tree and checked back again Sunday morning. Tira says it does not mean there was not a lion, as one was spotted in the Pac Heights area in January, captured and released back into the wild. “They typically come from the coast, from the Peninsula where there is a good population of lions and they can move up through the Peninsula up into wild habit, the wilder natural habitat, if you look at the map, the Panhandle is kind of connected to Golden Gate Park,” Tira said. He says it’s impossible to say where it went but the panhandle is connected to a lot of habitats leading all the way to the coast. So, the best-case scenario is that it follows the same path back. On Sunday, Animal Care and Control said there’s no longer a threat and it is believed the animal left the area. Hours later, authorities said someone reported a mountain lion sighting in the area of 44th and Fulton at 3 p.m.

headlines.title: 2 dead after SUV crashes into embankment in Solano County
headlines.description: Two people died after their vehicle left the road and crashed into an embankment in Solano County Sunday, the California Highway Patrol said. CHP said they received a 911 call just before 12:30 p.m. regarding a vehicle that had traveled off the roadway on eastbound Interstate 80 near the Highway 113 interchange. A preliminary investigation determined that a 2011 black Infiniti FX35 SUV was traveling eastbound on I-80 when it veered off the roadway and crashed into an embankment on the right shoulder, according to authorities. Authorities said the driver, who was a 56-year-old woman from Dixon, died at the scene, and the 65-year-old male passenger died while en route to the hospital. A witness to the crash reported that the driver appeared to be asleep at the wheel just before the SUV left the roadway, CHP said.

headlines.title: Fourth annual Lowrider Day returns to downtown San Jose
headlines.description: Lowriders will cruise into downtown San Jose this weekend, bringing a piece of East San Jose’s Chicano culture to City Hall for an afternoon of custom cars, music and celebration. San Jose Lowrider Day returns Sunday for its fourth year, marking the anniversary of the City Council’s decision to repeal a decades-old cruising ban. The celebration — hosted by the offices of Councilmembers Anthony Tordillos and Peter Ortiz, as well as the United Lowrider Council of San Jose — will run from noon to 6 p.m. on Santa Clara Street between Third and Seventh streets in front of City Hall. It will feature lowriders, live music, food and local vendors, community resources and performances throughout the afternoon. At a Tuesday meeting, councilmembers officially proclaimed Sunday as 2026 Lowrider Day. But for members of the United Lowrider Council of San Jose, the annual event is about more than showing off cars. Ricardo Cortez, a member of the lowrider council who handles history and youth education, said it’s an opportunity to reclaim a culture that has long been stereotyped as criminal and show how lowriding has become an important part of San Jose’s cultural identity. Negative stereotypes can cause people to make assumptions about people simply because of the cars they drive, he said. “I think it really comes down to being able to take back the negative narratives that have surrounded lowrider culture for a very long time,” Cortez told San Jose Spotlight. “I think every year it gets bigger. It gets more popular.” The lowrider council has tried to counter negative perceptions through community events and educational presentations at schools and colleges. Cortez teaches students about the origins of lowriding, historically significant cars, hydraulics and San Jose’s role in the culture. He also wrote a children’s book, “The ABCs of Lowriding,” that he uses in his presentations. “I think a lot of it has to come down to the older generation, meeting the youth where they’re at and trying to inspire them to want to continue this tradition,” Cortez said. The celebration also represents a shift in the city’s relationship with the culture of lowriders and cruising. Cruising has been part of Chicano culture since the 1940s, and grew to be a symbol of Mexican American resistance against discrimination during the civil rights movement of the 1960s and 70s. But by the 1990s it had become associated nationally with gang violence and illegal activity, leading to cities across the U.S., including San Jose, to create laws prohibiting cruising. San Jose had a cruising ban for decades before the city council repealed it in 2022, in part due to the efforts of police officer and then-Councilmember Raul Peralez, who experienced discrimination in his youth from the cruising ban. The annual Lowrider Day grew out of that change, David Polanco, president of the United Lowrider Council of San Jose, said. “(San Jose is not) the capital of lowriding, but we’re definitely a pillar of lowriding here within the lowrider world,” Polanco told San Jose Spotlight. Polanco said the lowrider council has worked to build relationships with city agencies, nonprofits, schools and other community organizations. The group also works with the San Jose Police Department when organizing events and cruises. Councilmember Ortiz, who grew up in East San Jose, said he remembers seeing lowriders in his neighborhood, particularly around King and Story roads and during Cinco de Mayo and other cultural celebrations. “We still, unfortunately, have a stigma in the greater community against lowriders,” Ortiz told San Jose Spotlight. He said many lowrider and cruising enthusiasts are working professionals with families, adding that public events can help residents see the people behind the cars rather than stereotypes. For Ortiz, bringing the celebration to City Hall and partnering with SJPD to plan events and organized cruises is part of that shift. “I’m just excited for our Chicano community to be full front here at City Hall, at the people’s house, to display the beautiful and significance of the Chicano culture here in the city of San Jose,” Ortiz said. Editor’s note: This story was originally published by San Jose Spotlight.

headlines.title: Police investigate fatal Friday night shooting in East Oakland
headlines.description: The Oakland Police Department is investigating a fatal shooting that occurred late Friday night in East Oakland. Officers responded to the 9300 block of Walter Avenue shortly after 10:45 p.m. on Friday following reports of an unresponsive person lying in the street, according to the Oakland Police Department. Upon arrival, police located an adult male suffering from apparent gunshot wounds. The victim died at the scene. The victim’s identity is being withheld pending the notification of next of kin. The OPD Homicide Section has launched a follow-up investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death. No further details have been released, and police said the case remains an ongoing investigation. Authorities are asking anyone with information, video, or photos related to the incident to contact the OPD Homicide Section at 510-238-3821 or the tip line at 510-238-7950. Visual evidence and tips can also be emailed to cidvideos@oaklandca.gov.

headlines.title: Woman dies after crash involving agricultural tractor in Brentwood
headlines.description: A woman died after a crash involving an agricultural tractor in Brentwood Saturday morning, the police department said. Police said officers responded to the area of Sand Creek and Shady Willow at around 6:16 a.m. regarding a crash involving a vehicle and an agricultural tractor. A 56-year-old woman, who was the driver and sole occupant of the vehicle, was pronounced at the scene, police reported. Authorities said the cause of the crash is under investigation.

headlines.title: Man accused of driving recklessly with a 3-year-old passenger in Santa Cruz County
headlines.description: A man was accused of driving recklessly and leading officers in a pursuit while having a 3-year-old child inside the vehicle, Capitola police said Saturday. On Friday night, police said officers attempted a traffic stop on an Acura sedan on 41st Avenue for a traffic violation. The driver did not stop and led officers on a pursuit, driving recklessly and going the wrong way at high speeds, according to authorities. Police said the pursuit was terminated in Aptos due to public safety concerns. Officials said a short time later, CHP units found the Acura near Seascape. When CHP attempted a second stop, the suspect drove away, initiating a second pursuit that ended when the vehicle stopped near Hidden Beach County Park, police said. The driver refused to exit the vehicle, and a barricade situation emerged, according to authorities. When the 41-year-old driver was taken into custody, police said officers found a 3-year-old passenger in the vehicle. The police department said the driver, a Las Vegas man, was arrested on suspicion of felony evading, DUI and child endangerment. The child’s mother, a woman from Las Vegas, was also taken into custody by CHP on separate charges. Police said the child was not injured and was turned over to protective services.

headlines.title: Authorities respond to multiple medical-related calls during concert in San Jose
headlines.description: More than a dozen people were taken to the hospital due to a variety of medical concerns during a concert at Discovery Meadow Friday night, authorities said. The San Jose Fire Department said it responded to an outdoor concert at Discovery Meadow at around 8:22 p.m. after receiving reports of multiple people requiring medical attention. According to authorities, a total of 14 ambulances responded, and 14 people were taken to local hospitals; previously, the police department said at least 10 people were taken to the hospital. The police department said these medical concerns also included “suspected alcohol intoxication and drug-related issues”.

headlines.title: Stabbing suspect arrested after fleeing into water near Baker Beach, police say
headlines.description: A stabbing suspect was taken into custody after allegedly trying to run away from law enforcement by entering the water near Baker Beach, police said. Police said officers responded at around 11:13 a.m. to the 100 block of Yacht Road regarding a stabbing. There, authorities said they found a person with an apparent stab wound. The victim was taken to the hospital for non-life-threatening injuries. Police said the suspect ran away and jumped into the water near Baker Beach. According to authorities, the suspect was taken into custody by the police department’s Marine Unit.

headlines.title: Pittsburg PD officer shot by suspect who snuck gun into police station: report
headlines.description: The suspect accused of shooting a police officer inside the Pittsburg police station Thursday had snuck a gun into the station, according to the East Bay Times. Pittsburg police say an officer was booking a 31-year-old suspect on Thursday when the two got into an altercation and a gun was fired. Both men were hit. NBC Bay Area reached out to the police chief, asking how a gun made it into the booking area, but have not received a response. However, the East Bay Times reported the suspect somehow snuck the gun in. According to law enforcement analyst Michael Leininger, the typical protocol is that suspects are searching for weapons and officers secure their own firearms before entering the booking area. “When you take the handcuffs off an individual, they now have a certain amount of flexibility that they did not have, and if they want to take you on, you’ve enabled that by removing the handcuffs,” he said. The East Bay Times also reported the suspect then assaulted police and is now jailed on suspicion of attempted murder of a peace officer. Mayor Dionne Adams says she wants the investigation to play out. “I don’t know the protocols because I’m not an officer and I can’t really speak to what happened because I don’t know what happened and when, all I know is one of our officers is injured,” Adams said. So far, no update on the officer’s condition. As for the shooting, it remains under investigation by Pittsburg police and the Contra Costa County DA’s Office.

headlines.title: California gas prices surge during Labor Day weekend
headlines.description: According to AAA, the average price of gas in California for this Labor Day weekend is $5.81, which is about $1.20 more expensive than a year ago. According to AAA, the average in California is climbing, right ahead of Labor Day weekend. Fuel prices are increasing as the war with Iran continues. “There’s no real sign of change in the war in the middle east and that is the main driver of the spike in gas prices, so I don’t think we’re likely to see any real relief in the next few weeks,” Energy Institute at Haas, UC Berkeley Faculty Director Severin Borenstein said. Borenstein says it’s difficult to predict what the price at the pump could look like in a few months too because so much of it is driven by the war. Jocelyn Moran has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: Investigation underway after officer shot at Pittsburg police station
headlines.description: A police officer is recovering after getting shot inside a Pittsburg police station. The shooting occurred at the department’s booking room Thursday after what police are calling an altercation between an officer and a suspect when a gun was discharged, wounding both of them. Pittsburg police did not provide any further information about the incident on Friday, but policing experts said the shooting would not have happened if basic protocol had been followed. “There is one thing that is beyond dispute,” policing expert Michael Leininger said. “There was a significant mistake that was made.” Pittsburg Sep 3 Richmond Sep 3 Leininger said basic protocol to ensure a suspect is unarmed before bringing him inside a booking room, where fingerprints and phots are taken. Officers must also lock up their own weapons before entering. “When you take the handcuffs off an individual, they have a certain amount of flexibility that they did not have. And if they want to take you on, you’ve enabled them by removing the handcuffs,” Leininger said. “And you should not do that until you’re 100% certain that they do not have any weapons, and you yourself do not have any weapons.” NBC Bay Area reached out to the Pittsburg police chief specifically asking how a gun ended up in the booking room and who it belonged to, but did not receive a response Friday. Meanwhile, Mayor Dionne Adams is asking residents to pray for the officer, who is in serious condition. “All I know is one of our officers was injured,” Adams said. “And we’re continually praying to make sure he pulls through safely and he gets home to his family.” The mayor also said he could not share any new information on what led to the shooting, but assured the community a full investigation is underway. “I’m deeply saddened by what happened here and want to assure the community Pittsburg still remains a safe city,” Adams said. “I think the lesson here is that things happen. We want to make sure we know all the details before we come to conclusions.”

headlines.title: Emergency crews respond to hazardous materials incident in San Francisco
headlines.description: Emergency crews responded to a hazardous materials incident Friday in San Francisco. The San Francisco Fire Department said the incident involved muriatic acid and chlorine at the Presidio Golf and Concordia Golf Course. At least one person was taken to a hospital due to the incident. Hazardous materials units and fire crews responded to the scene to investigate. Residents and the public were asked to avoid the area.
